finding: Death-bowling order lists a batter first: Abdul Samad is named top death bowler in the bowling plan
evidence: step5_bowling_plan.csv Death row = 'Abdul Samad, Brijesh Sharma, Xavier Bartlett'. Samad has 3 legal balls bowled in 2023-26 (all Death), so his share-of-own-balls in Death is 100% and he outranks real bowlers. Code ranks by ph_use share of own overs, not by volume. Same flaw pads Middle/Powerplay rows.
suggested_fix: Rank by balls bowled in the phase (or require a minimum bowling workload, e.g. bowl_share>=0.5 already used for the XI) and drop non-bowlers; regenerate bowling plan.

finding: Two of the three Must-Back players are not in Plan A or the XI, yet headlines say 'Back X, Y, Z first'
evidence: Must-Back = Ashutosh Sharma, Pathirana, Cummins. Plan A = Ashutosh, Rizvi, Samad, Vyshak, Bartlett, Mohsin; XI has none of Pathirana/Cummins. They are chosen by interval floor (lo80>=50; only 3 pool players pass) with fit_weight 0.6, i.e. the model itself rates them below Samad/Iyer. Cheat sheet heading (step7_docs) says 'Back {must} first'.
suggested_fix: Either rename tier (e.g. 'Highest-evidence names') or let the optimiser force Must-Backs; explain why a Must-Back that fills no measured gap is not in Plan A; make the tier rule and the optimiser agree.

finding: Gap measurement is far inside noise, yet it drives fit_weight (1.5 vs 0.6) and so the whole optimiser
evidence: Reproduced RR-group High-pressure 2025-26: Batting Middle -9.71 vs league -2.38 per 100 on 243 balls; Death +3.86 vs +7.01 on 359 balls. Per-100 standard errors from ball-level sd: 10.7 (Middle), 10.1 (Death). Gaps -7.3 and -3.2 are well under 1 SE. Death split by season: 2025 -15.8 (247 balls) vs 2026 +47.2 (112). step5_gaps.csv carries no SE or interval. Checkpoint says 'RR's bowling is above league in every phase' but bowling gaps +1.8/+5.7/+7.1 have SE 9-12.
suggested_fix: Add bootstrap-by-match interval and a 'not distinguishable from league' flag to step5_gaps; soften 'gap'/'above league' wording; use a sensitivity run with equal fit weights to show whether Plan A changes.

finding: Plan A is feasible only at band midpoints; at walk-away prices it costs Rs 23 cr against the assumed Rs 15 cr purse
evidence: Plan A walk_away_cr sum = 3+3+8+3+3+3 = 23.0. Optimiser uses mid=(lo+hi)/2 (13.75 total) while the stated 'walk-away' is top of band. Purse is slack (1.25 cr unused); slots (6), not money, are binding, so this is not really a budget optimisation. Brute force itself is correct: my independent enumeration reproduces Plan A, Plan B and value 5.4165/5.4157, with purse<=15 and overseas<=2 respected.
suggested_fix: State the worst-case cost; run the optimiser on walk-away prices as a stress case; say plainly that the purse is not binding under assumed bands.

finding: Squad arithmetic breaks the script's own reported limits (A5/A9 vs F1-006/007/024)
evidence: XI/bench pool = 20 RR 2026 players + 6 Plan A signings = 26 > 25 max (F1-006). Data-inferred overseas in RR group = 7 (Archer, Burger, Hetmyer, Ferreira, Shanaka, Milne, Pretorius) + Bartlett = 8 = the cap; A5 says 'up to 2 overseas' open slots, which would breach 8 (F1-024 says RR had 8 overseas at the end of the 2026 auction). Plan A's 6 slots assume 19 retained, but the XI keeps all 20.
suggested_fix: Make the XI/bench squad = assumed retained set (<=19) + signings; derive open overseas slots from the same retained set (8 - overseas retained) instead of the fixed 2; flag in A5.

finding: Plan B is not a meaningful 'if X goes past walk-away' rule
evidence: step5_plan_b: if Abdul Samad > Rs 8 cr, switch to Venkatesh Iyer; rr_loses '0%'. Values 5.4165 vs 5.4157 (difference 0.0009, a rounding tie). 'Top target' is chosen as the highest-priced Plan A member (Samad, mid 5.5), not the most valuable (Ashutosh, value 1.48). Iyer has the same Rs 3-8 cr band so a price spike that hits Samad is equally likely to hit Iyer; swap exchanges a death-over finisher (Death gap) for a top-order bat (Middle gap), which '0% lost' hides. If Ashutosh passes Rs 3 cr (the most likely stress) Plan B falls to 4.14 (-24%) and is not reported.
suggested_fix: Define the top target by value contribution; provide a Plan B per top-3 target; report what is lost in role terms (finisher vs top order) and the value change with a tolerance; say 'tie' when delta is below noise.

finding: Plan A buys three more pacers although the same script says RR bowling is above league in every phase
evidence: Plan A = 3 batters + Vyshak, Bartlett, Mohsin (all pace). Bowlers get x0.6 but any positive value fills a free slot because there is no minimum-value or need threshold; slots, not need, drive it. RR already has Archer, Burger, Sandeep, Brijesh, Deshpande. XI then has 5 pacers and Jadeja as sole spinner.
suggested_fix: Add a cap per role or a need constraint (e.g. only gap-filling players or max 1 bowler); or allow leaving slots empty when marginal value is below a threshold.

finding: Availability proxy A3 (top-6 involvement per team in 2026) is applied but is demonstrably crude; availability for the shortlist is unverified for all 10
evidence: All 10 shortlisted, all contrarian/avoid/unsung and all optimiser players are 'UNKNOWN [A2]' (tagged, so consistent with rules, none VERIFIED). Proxy misclassifies: Cummins (SRH) ranks 9th by 2026 involvement so is not 'core'; Shivam Dube (CSK) rank 7, Mukesh Kumar rank 7, Prasidh rank 9 not core; Rohit Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav, Rinku Singh, Nicholas Pooran, David Miller, Boult labelled 'In auction pool'. Five of the F1-026 Nov 2026 trade players (Livingstone, Khaleel, Natarajan, Pant, Kuldeep) have stale latest_team and A3 does not use the REPORTED trades. Core flag is also ignored for the unsung pick.
suggested_fix: Use F1-026 trades to update teams; treat captains/established stars as retained; add 'Player unlikely to reach pool' label for avoid/contrarian lists; use the same pool filter for unsung; foreground that every name is conditional.

finding: Theekshana is tagged RR in 2025 but shown as 'In auction pool'; Pathirana played 8 balls in 2026
evidence: Theekshana: latest_team RR, latest_season 2025, availability 'In auction pool: UNKNOWN' (not in RR group, not core): status as an RR-contracted/ex-RR player is untested (also Hasaranga, Madhwal). Pathirana (score 98.4, 180 High balls) has only 8 legal balls for KKR in 2026 (19th in team); risk tags say only 'age UNKNOWN; injury UNKNOWN', no 'barely played 2026 / form-fitness' flag. Ashwin and Dhoni (latest_season 2025) are also 'In auction pool'.
suggested_fix: Add risk tag from recent involvement (e.g. 2026 balls < 25% of prior seasons) and a separate availability class for latest_season<2026 and ex-RR players.

finding: Hidden Gem tier is the smallest-sample players, not hidden quality
evidence: Gems = score>=60 sorted by hi_balls ascending: Bartlett 62 balls (floor is 60), Mohsin 113, Theekshana 132; interval floors 25.1, 38.7, 26.0 and widths 61-69. Sorting ascending by sample selects the noisiest estimates.
suggested_fix: Rank Gems by lower bound or by low-profile proxy (popularity) subject to a minimum sample; report sample size on each card.

finding: Nationality inference A7 leaves well-known internationals as UNKNOWN and silently treats UNKNOWN as Indian in the XI/optimiser
evidence: 23 candidates are 'UNKNOWN (no international data)' including Sunil Narine (West Indies), Faf du Plessis (South Africa), M S Dhoni, Sai Sudharsan, Ajinkya Rahane, Krunal Pandya, Ishant Sharma, Mohit Sharma, Jaydev Unadkat, Natarajan, Padikkal (capped for India per general knowledge). The dataset's non-IPL coverage is therefore partial. Code: squad.overseas_b = nat.get(...)[1] fillna(False) and optimiser overseas.fillna(False) count UNKNOWN as Indian. Shortlist cards for Rizvi, Samad, Mohsin therefore show 'UNKNOWN' and no capped/uncapped label (required by Step 5). Rahul Chahar 'Indian (India A in data)' while he is capped per general knowledge (suspected); cap status for 'India A' players is unsupported.
suggested_fix: Drop 'capped' wording where only absence of evidence; mark UNKNOWN players as 'UNKNOWN - could count as overseas' in overseas totals (worst case); add nationality/cap override list tagged [ASSUMPTION]; manually tag the few UNKNOWNs on the shortlist.

finding: Price bands ignore reputation and look implausibly low for stars; Cummins/Pathirana get Rs 3-7 cr
evidence: A6 tier = number of 2023-26 seasons with >=10 matches only. Cummins (injury-hit seasons) and Pathirana land in 'Regular' Rs 3-7 cr; Ashutosh Rs 0.3-3 cr; Shardul 0.3-3; Rizvi 0.3-3. General knowledge (unverified): Cummins and Pathirana were multi-crore (well above Rs 7 cr) buys and Ashutosh a retained player above Rs 3 cr. Walk-away = top of band, so walk-away is not a market ceiling and Plan A feasibility depends on it. Tagged [ASSUMPTION A6], so rule-compliant, but the bands drive every Plan A/B result.
suggested_fix: Anchor bands on the last observed price where available (tag as REPORTED with source) or widen bands and run optimiser sensitivity; add overseas/captain premium; say bands are 'play-count tiers', not valuations.

finding: Sample XI has no opener at 1 or 3, Jaiswal benched, and a keeper with score 7.3 hard-coded without explanation
evidence: xi.csv bat_order values: 2,4,5,6,7,7,8,10,10,10,11 (ties, no 1 and 3, the sort is by median position not a batting order). Jaiswal (RR top-order, score 39, interval 14-75), Parag and the batting-type balance are not in the XI; all 6 Plan A signings are first-choice. Dhruv Jurel (score 7.3, 0.6-37.4, 330 balls in 2026) is forced in as keeper (A11 hard-code). Mohsin Khan bats at 11, Sandeep Sharma is the Impact Player (a 6th pace bowler, bench top by score) with no batting cover. Only Jadeja bowls spin. No text explains any of this; lhb_in_xi in step7_payload is hard-coded to 0 (`and False`).
suggested_fix: Assign explicit order 1-11 (two openers), explain benching of Jaiswal/Parag by score and sample, show the XI with and without forced keeper, choose Impact Player as batter/bowler swap with a stated rule, and fix lhb_in_xi.

finding: Powerplay batting +52.9 per 100 is one rookie, and the group mixes players and seasons
evidence: RR-group Powerplay 228 balls: Sooryavanshi 85 balls contribute +78 runs above expected (about 92 per 100); 2025 +83 (126 balls) vs 2026 +22 (102). Group = all 20 players with 2026 RR involvement (including not-scorable fringe and anyone who may be traded or released) and includes their 2025 balls for other franchises (e.g. Jadeja).
suggested_fix: Report group composition and per-player contribution; show gap with and without the single largest contributor; label group as '2026 RR players, 2025-26 balls, any team'.

finding: Unsung hero rests on 62 High-pressure balls while contrarian is condemned on 95; asymmetric evidence bar
evidence: Unsung Bartlett: score 75.9 (25.1-91.1), 62 balls, wkts 4 in 2025-26; he is also Hidden Gem, in Plan A and the XI. Contrarians: Prasidh 2.1 (0.1-43.6, 95 balls), Shardul 5.7 (0.5-48.3, 175 balls). Unsung is chosen among all non-RR players (core not excluded, unlike shortlist).
suggested_fix: Require same minimum sample/interval floor for unsung (e.g. lo80>=40 and balls>=100) and exclude likely-retained; note that the unsung pick overlaps with a Hidden Gem.

finding: Contrarian pair rests on volume, not popularity, and contradicts a headline narrative without explanation
evidence: popularity_proxy = percentile of 2025-26 wickets/runs (bowlers by wickets, everyone else by runs, all-rounders' wickets ignored). Prasidh Krishna is reported (general knowledge, unverified) as a 2025 high wicket-taker; step5 shows score 2.1 with no explanation of the divergence (e.g. economy vs expected). Both picks are Indian pacers; no batter. Hi interval top 43.6 and 48.3 only just below 50. Tables contain no one-line reason/tone text; wording lives only in step7 docs ('Popular but low score').
suggested_fix: Add explanation columns (the two hard stats) and a respectful one-line reason per contrarian/avoid name; show why score and reputation diverge; state the proxy.

finding: Not-to-chase list has no per-name reason and mixes statistically weak cases
evidence: step5_not_to_chase.csv has no reason column; cheat sheet prints name + score + range only. Criteria score<30 and hi80<60 admit Mukesh Kumar (0.4-42.8) and Shivam Dube (1.9-35.2) whose intervals reach above median. Dube/Mukesh are also likely retained by their franchises (not in A3 core, because rank 7), so 'do not chase' may be moot.
suggested_fix: Add reason column (score, interval, sample, price band); require hi80<40 for 'avoid'; drop names probably retained.

finding: Spot-check of nationality A7: no overseas/Indian reversal found among 110 candidates
evidence: Checked 34 inferred overseas and 53 inferred Indian against general knowledge, including Cummins, Pathirana, Bartlett, Theekshana, Hetmyer, Archer, Burger, Ferreira (overseas) and Jadeja, Iyer, Prasidh, Mukesh, Dube, Sooryavanshi (Indian). All consistent. Residual weakness is coverage (above), not sign errors.
suggested_fix: None (passed); keep as note.

finding: Price, purse, slot and nationality numerics appear untagged in numeric columns that flow downstream
evidence: price_lo_cr/price_hi_cr/walk_away_cr/mid and purse_assumed_cr are plain numbers; only the price_band string carries [ASSUMPTION A6]. step7_payload exposes price_mid and walk_away without tags; xi.overseas_b has no tag; Impact Player rule (F1-014 REPORTED) and keeper (A11) are not tagged in the XI/xi_meta files. Assumption numbering A11 precedes A10.
suggested_fix: Add a 'basis' column (A6/A4/A9/A11) to plans, xi and xi_meta; renumber assumptions.

finding: XI passes basic constraints
evidence: 11 players, 2 overseas (Archer, Bartlett) <= 4, Dhruv Jurel as keeper (tagged A11), 6 bowling options, no duplicates. Output reproducible: rerun of step5_auction.py leaves all outputs/tables unchanged.
suggested_fix: None (passed).

finding: Step 5 requirements not met: age, left/right balance, spin and overseas-slot gaps are not measured; no per-player case text in step5 tables
evidence: Gap table covers phase batting/bowling only; rr_group has batting type and pace/spin columns but no left-right or spin gap row; age UNKNOWN for all (A8). Shortlist/contrarian/unsung/avoid CSVs have no 3-line case, hard stats or how-he-strengthens-the-XI text (only in step7 renderings, where cheat sheet shows tier, score, price, risk and gap only).
suggested_fix: Add left-right, spin and overseas-slot rows to the gap table as [ASSUMPTION] or measured; add case columns to step5 tables (2 hard stats each).

finding: Wording of Plan A 'narrows/improves the gap' and 'RR loses X% of pressure value' implies projection, against D15
evidence: step7_docs: 'Plan A improves both measured batting gaps ... on only a few added High-pressure balls' and OPEN_GAP/FIT before->after (past balls of added players pooled with RR's); plan_b 'rr_loses' reports a percentage of an invented value (score x 1.5/0.6). Hedge 'direction, not proof' exists but the unsmoothed numbers still read as forecast. Backtest ability to predict is not established (D15).
suggested_fix: Phrase as 'past rates of the added players would have been...'; drop the percentage or label it as an index with no units.

finding: Likely-retained proxy applied consistently for shortlist/optimiser/avoid but not for contrarian or unsung
evidence: pool = cand minus in_rr_2026 minus likely_retained_core feeds shortlist, optimiser, avoid. contrarian and unsung use cand (no core filter). No current conflict in outputs (neither is core), but the rule is not enforced and RR's own players are excluded from unsung only via ~in_rr_2026.
suggested_fix: Use pool for unsung; for contrarian state they are 'names RR should not pay up for', independent of availability.

finding: Passed checks
evidence: Re-run identical; gap per-100 arithmetic matches independent recomputation (High bucket, 2025-26 seasons, group vs league, sign: batting RAE positive good, bowling RSE positive good = runs saved, consistent with league means of opposite sign); shortlist excludes RR-2026 and core-proxy players; tiers follow the coded rules (3/4/3, 10 names); brute-force optimiser respects purse, 6 slots, 2 overseas; not-scorable list correctly excludes sample-poor players (D3).
